record.original_question: Suppose f (z) = z + ∞ n n=2 an z is univalent and bounded by M in D. Find sup max |sn (eit )|, t 0≤t≤2π where n X sn (z) = z + ak z k . k=2 (F. Holland)

evidence.quote: Suppose f (z) = z + ∞ n n=2 an z is univalent and bounded by M in D. Find sup max |sn (eit )|, t 0≤t≤2π where n X sn (z) = z + ak z k . k=2 (F. Holland)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk. Fix $M>1$ and let $\mathcal{S}(M)$ be the family of functions
$$f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_n z^n$$
that are holomorphic and univalent (one-to-one) in $\mathbb{D}$ and satisfy $|f(z)|\le M$ for all $z\in\mathbb{D}$. For each integer $n\ge 2$, let
$$s_n(z)=z+\sum_{k=2}^{n}a_k z^k$$
denote the $n$-th partial sum (section) of the Taylor expansion of $f$. Determine, as a function of $M$ and $n$,
$$\Phi(M,n)\;=\;\sup_{f\in\mathcal{S}(M)}\;\max_{0\le t\le 2\pi}\bigl|s_n(e^{it})\bigr|.$$
artifact.category_tag: Bounded univalent functions and Taylor sections
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published work that explicitly determines this supremum for bounded univalent functions on the unit disk. No result by F. Holland or others giving an exact formula for $\sup_{f}\max_{t}|s_n(e^{it})|$ in this setting was found, so the current status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The sum of coefficients of bounded univalent functions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses coefficient sums for bounded univalent functions but does not address the maximum modulus of partial sums on the unit circle.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on bounded univalent functions exist, but none located gives the exact supremum sought.

status_evidence.title: Coefficient characterizations and sections for some univalent functions
status_evidence.snippet: Treats sections of univalent functions, but not the specific extremal problem for bounded univalent f.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit solution to the stated extremal problem was found.
